summary: The agent did load hyperpowers:brainstorming. But it explicitly called the ambiguous brief "bounded", put a short design in chat, never wrote a spec document, and went straight to editing app.js once I approved. The router did not escalate to the architectural path.
reasoning: Criterion 1 passes: the Skill call happened before any edits. Criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail. The agent said "Classification: **bounded**" and skipped the spec document, and no docs/ directory exists in the workdir. The odd part is that it recognised the hidden complexity in its own words ("That's an interface decision others would build against, and it's the expensive one to reverse") and still did not escalate. Criterion 5 passes because it did not treat this as a spike.

observations.description: The router's classification contradicts the agent's own analysis. It wrote "That's an interface decision others would build against, and it's the expensive one to reverse" and noted the change affects the public login() signature and how tracking IDs work downstream. It still classified the task as bounded and skipped the spec. The architectural signals were recognised but did not trigger escalation.

The bounded call seems to rest on the narrow reason that the function has one caller: "login() already exists in app.js and has one caller". It ignored the cross-cutting concern it had just described itself, which is a persistent localStorage identity scheme that other code will depend on.
The clarifying question (userId source, 3 options plus a recommendation) was well framed and honestly explained the trade-offs, e.g. that the ID identifies a browser, not a person.
Launcher setup: the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to "No, exit", so one careless Enter kills the run. There were also blank screens of a few seconds between the dialogs.
After approval the agent's only check was a syntax check (`node --check app.js`). It said there is no test harness, so verification was manual.

criteria.evidence: First tool_use in the session log: {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}. The Edit calls came later, after my approval.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before asking for approval
criteria.evidence: Assistant text: "Classification: **bounded** — `login()` already exists in `app.js` and has one caller, so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec." `ls coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned "No such file or directory". git status shows only " M app.js".

criteria.criterion: Spec document presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: No spec file was created. What I was asked to approve was a "Short design" in chat ending with "Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go." The tool calls in the log are Skill, Bash, Read, AskUserQuestion, Read, Edit, Edit, Bash. There is no Write to a specs path.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec doc
criteria.evidence: It did exactly that: it announced "bounded", gave an in-chat design, and after "looks good, go ahead" it made two Edit calls on app.js, with no committed spec (git log shows only the fixture commits).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: The classification text says "bounded", not spike. No probe plan was offered, and the approval gate was a short design, not a feasibility probe.
